text:
The U.S. Constitution is the supreme law of the land. Federal statutes and treaties rank beneath it and are coequal with each other, so the later enactment controls when they conflict, and both, together with valid federal regulations issued under statute, prevail over conflicting state law. State constitutions come next, then state statutes, state regulations, and local ordinances. Courts interpret each level and invalidate any lower law that contradicts a higher one.

CONFIDENCE: 95
